source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 7 (The Modern Indian Art).

sections.heading: 1. Beyond the Bengal School
points: By the 1920s–40s, Indian artists moved **beyond the Bengal School's revivalism** toward **modernism** (individual expression, modern Western techniques + Indian roots).
Modern Indian art absorbed **Cubism, Expressionism and abstraction** while retaining Indian themes.

sections.heading: 2. Pioneers of Modernism
points: **Rabindranath Tagore** — painted expressive, spontaneous works late in life.
**Amrita Sher-Gil** — a pioneering modernist; blended European technique with Indian subjects (village life, women).
**Jamini Roy** — drew on **Bengal folk (Kalighat) art**; bold flat forms.
**Nandalal Bose** — bridged the Bengal School and modern art.

sections.heading: 3. The Progressive Artists' Group
points: The **Progressive Artists' Group (Bombay, 1947)** launched Indian modern art onto the world stage.
Members: **F.N. Souza, S.H. Raza, M.F. Husain, K.H. Ara, S.K. Bakre, H.A. Gade**.
**M.F. Husain** ('Picasso of India') became India's most famous modern painter; **S.H. Raza** known for the **'Bindu'** abstraction.

sections.heading: 4. Sculpture, Printmaking and After
points: Modern **sculpture** — **Ramkinkar Baij** (Santiniketan), a pioneer of modern Indian sculpture.
Printmaking and new media developed; artists like **Tyeb Mehta, K.G. Subramanyan, Anjolie Ela Menon** contributed.
Modern Indian art is diverse — combining **global modernism with Indian identity**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Amrita Sher-Gil = pioneer modernist (European technique + Indian subjects).
Jamini Roy = inspired by Bengal folk/Kalighat art.
Progressive Artists' Group (Bombay, 1947): Souza, Raza, Husain, Ara, Bakre, Gade.
M.F. Husain = 'Picasso of India'; S.H. Raza = 'Bindu'.
Ramkinkar Baij = pioneer of modern Indian sculpture (Santiniketan).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Progressive Artists' Group** was founded in **Bombay in 1947**.
**Amrita Sher-Gil** is a pioneering modern Indian painter.
**Jamini Roy** drew on **Bengal folk (Kalighat)** art.
**S.H. Raza** is associated with the **'Bindu'** (point) motif.
